correctness.rationale: If both members of a position are omitted, every possible original witness for its duplicate also sees the omitted original; hence only three omission symbols are needed. A neighboring original witness must itself be selected and see no omission at its other neighboring position; a duplicate witness works only for an original omission and must see no other original omission. These are exactly the two clauses in the radius-two rule, including nonexisting path positions. The cyclic wrap for n=4 remains valid. The independent reconstruction reproduced the displayed potential, all 178 arcs on 81 states, all 90 tight arcs, three simple tight cycles of length eight, and boundary state counts 46 each with maxima −2 and 4. Summing 4w−3≤Δh around a cyclic walk gives the 3n/4 omission bound. Equality forces the entire walk to be tight; decomposition into the checked simple cycles requires an order divisible by eight. For the path, the initial four positions contribute explicitly, and the boundary maxima yield floor((3n+2)/4). Direct graph-level enumeration of 174,672 omission subsets for paths of orders 2–8 and cycles 4–8 confirms the small cases and the four-omission maximum for P6. All 14 path and 8 cycle seeds and the necessary eight-step returns were checked. Inserting at a shared four-symbol state adds six omissions in eight positions while preserving all local constraints and endpoints; induction on each residue class, not the finite sample through order 64, proves attainment for arbitrary orders.
